findings.highlight: the scene in the dressing room flickering in my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 脱衣場での一件がちらついて
findings.governingReading: The dressing-room incident keeps flashing across Shirou’s mind and prevents him tasting dinner.
findings.explanation: “The scene … flickering” is mechanical English that weakens the intrusive-memory effect.

findings.highlight: learn magic from Rin
findings.evidenceJa: 凛に魔術を教わる
findings.governingReading: Shirou promised to receive magecraft instruction from Rin at night.
findings.explanation: The work’s technical practice becomes generic magic.

findings.highlight: As soon as I enter the room, I see Tohsaka doing something weird.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂は宝石らしきものを手のひらに置いて
findings.governingReading: The active narration begins directly with the jewel, syringe, and handkerchief arrangement.
findings.explanation: The English inserts timing and an evaluative reaction absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: Folf on. I’ll fe fone fife fofei’s fife fith.
findings.evidenceJa: ひょっひまっへ。きょふののるまはこれへおはりだから
findings.governingReading: Through the handkerchief, Rin says to wait a moment because this will finish today’s quota.
findings.explanation: The phonetic distortion becomes nearly unrecoverable gibberish, losing the quota and completion information.

findings.highlight: putting that aside
findings.evidenceJa: 向いてるか向いてないかは別にして
findings.governingReading: Shirou contrasts Rin with Saber, then explicitly reserves judgment on whether Rin is actually suited to teaching.
findings.explanation: The vague transition drops his distinction between eagerness and teaching aptitude.

findings.highlight: The magics of my family are flow and conversion of power
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の魔術は力の流動と転換
findings.governingReading: Tohsaka magecraft specializes in the flow and conversion of power.
findings.explanation: Plural “magics” and a generic family paraphrase obscure a named inherited technical specialty.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka concludes the conversation, leaving me way behind.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の魔力を余所に移しておくのよ
findings.governingReading: Rin’s active line ends after explaining that she transfers spare magical energy elsewhere.
findings.explanation: The English adds a narration sentence absent from the active Japanese and falsely says the conversation concludes.

findings.highlight: jewels are easy targets to transfer magical energy into
findings.evidenceJa: 宝石は魔力を溜めやすい物
findings.governingReading: Jewels readily accumulate and retain magical energy.
findings.explanation: The English recasts a material storage property as ease of targeting a transfer.

findings.highlight: turns the jewels themselves into ‘magic’
findings.evidenceJa: 宝石自体を“魔術”にする
findings.governingReading: Years of accumulation turn the jewel itself into a stored magecraft.
findings.explanation: Generic “magic” blurs the distinction between magical energy and a prepared spell-like working.

findings.highlight: instantly activate a large-scale magic
findings.evidenceJa: 大魔術を瞬間的に発動
findings.governingReading: The stored energy serves as ignition for instantaneous activation of great magecraft.
findings.explanation: The English uses nonstandard “a magic” and defines greatness only as physical scale.

findings.highlight: the only other magus I know is Kiritsugu
findings.evidenceJa: そんな便利なコト、なんで他の魔術師はしないんだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks why other magi do not use this convenient storage method.
findings.explanation: The English restores an extra comparator sentence absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: is unique
findings.evidenceJa: 特殊なのよ
findings.governingReading: Storing magical energy outside oneself is a special technique.
findings.explanation: “Unique” promotes a marked or unusual method into an absolute claim that no one else can possess it.

findings.highlight: She murmurs to herself.
findings.evidenceJa: なら確かにしょうがないか
findings.governingReading: Rin quietly reasons through why Shirou truly had to begin from scratch.
findings.explanation: The English adds an explicit murmuring action absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: Haven’t you realized that I don’t have a Magic Crest?
findings.evidenceJa: 随分前に気が付いてたんじゃないのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether Rin had noticed the missing crest long before now.
findings.explanation: The English loses the “long ago” premise that her shocked response then refutes.

findings.highlight: listen up
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと腰を落ち着かせて聞くこと
findings.governingReading: Rin orders Shirou to sit down properly and settle in because the explanation matters.
findings.explanation: The English keeps attention but removes the deliberate seated posture and lesson tone.

findings.highlight: there are some that that use magic
findings.evidenceJa: 自分以外の代価をもって魔術を使用する者
findings.governingReading: Some practitioners perform magecraft by supplying a price external to themselves.
findings.explanation: The duplicated “that” visibly corrupts the sentence.

findings.highlight: Then, let’s start with magic that uses the large source.
findings.evidenceJa: 大源を用いた魔術から順に説明しましょう
findings.governingReading: Rin proposes beginning with magecraft that uses Mana, the Greater Source.
findings.explanation: The English leaves the spoken passage without a closing quotation mark.

findings.highlight: make contact with the divine mystery
findings.evidenceJa: 神秘と接触する方法
findings.governingReading: Formal Craft uses established ritual and offerings to make contact with Mystery.
findings.explanation: The English adds “divine,” narrowing a technical concept to religious divinity.

findings.highlight: spend the whole evening praying
findings.evidenceJa: 一晩中祈る
findings.governingReading: Shirou rejects praying in a magic circle all night.
findings.explanation: The English shortens the duration from the entire night to the evening.

findings.highlight: put their hands on’ that magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術が“手に取れる”
findings.governingReading: A mastered magecraft becomes something the magus can figuratively take in hand as part of the self.
findings.explanation: The plural-handed English idiom suggests obtaining or seizing an object and remains unnatural.

findings.highlight: perhaps this crest I will give you might offer some help
findings.evidenceJa: もしかしたらワシが残した刻印が何かの役に立つかもしれん
findings.governingReading: Rin performs an old magus’s voice: perhaps the crest this old man leaves will help the heir.
findings.explanation: The English removes the mock-aged first person and flattens her quoted performance.

findings.highlight: Cursing in a disappointed manner
findings.evidenceJa: やれやれと悪態をついて
findings.governingReading: Rin grumbles exasperatedly about people who know magecraft only abstractly yet try to use it.
findings.explanation: The English combines emotion and action into an unnatural phrase that blunts her disdain.

findings.highlight: medical tools
findings.evidenceJa: 矯正器具
findings.governingReading: Rin ominously mentions medicine and corrective apparatus for altering Shirou’s internal operation.
findings.explanation: The English broadens a device meant to correct or force alignment into generic medical tools.

findings.highlight: I’m going to suffer as well
findings.evidenceJa: わたしたちまで被害を受ける
findings.governingReading: Rin warns that conflict between Shirou and Saber during battle would harm Rin’s side as well.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the affected group to Rin personally.

findings.highlight: I hate being indirect like you
findings.evidenceJa: もともと口べたなんだよ、俺は
findings.governingReading: Shirou refuses the advice by saying he has always been a poor talker.
findings.explanation: The English inserts hostility toward Rin’s indirectness, making his reply more personally combative.
